anomalies.observed: On power.kicad_sch, the +12V rail is connected to pin 1 of both fan headers (J7 and J8), and the tachometer signals FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH are connected to pin 2 of J7 / J8 respectively (pin 3 = no-connect, pin 4 = GND).
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the fan-header 12 V pins are J7/J8 pin 2 (consistent with the standard 4-pin fan pinout: pin1=GND, pin2=+12V, pin3=tach). The +12V net must therefore sit on pin 2, not pin 1, and the tach signal must not be on pin 2.

evidence.quote: Also on this net: ... the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2) [on the +12V net] — power.kicad_sch / controller.net, Section 3 Inputs
power.kicad_sch (sheet /Power/, page 3/4): J7 Conn_01x04_Pin pin 1 -> +12V arrow, pin 2 -> FAN_0_TACH; J8 pin 1 -> +12V arrow, pin 2 -> FAN_1_TACH

anomalies.impact: A standard 4-pin fan plugged into J7/J8 receives +12V on its GND pin (board pin 1) and the 3.3V tach pull-up on its +12V pin (board pin 2), while its tach output (fan pin 3) lands on the board's no-connect pin. The fans will not run, the tach inputs will read the wrong node, fan-stall fault detection is defeated, and the 3.3V-referenced tach line / TVS may be over-stressed.

parsed.summary: The drawing matches the specification on every explicitly checkable value, part identity and power-path connection (TPS2121 mux, AP63203 buck, TPS1H200 heater switch, MAX31855 channels, USB-C pulldowns, R12/C5, etc.), but the two fan headers J7/J8 are wired with +12V on pin 1 and the tach signal on pin 2, contradicting the spec's explicit statement that the fan-header 12V pins are pin 2 — a connector pin-assignment error that would stop the fans and break tach/fault monitoring.
